answer: According to the European Commission against Racism and Intolerance's 2018 work on algorithmic decision-making, AI-driven discrimination can slip past existing anti-discrimination laws because the majority of non-discrimination statutes relate only to specific protected characteristics. There are other forms of discrimination that are not correlated with protected characteristics but can still reinforce social inequality. This means that AI systems can exploit gaps in the legal framework, allowing discriminatory practices to occur without direct violations of existing laws.
